teaser: I kept promising myself a quieter year.
reflection: I kept promising myself a quieter year. You would ask me to sit beside you, and I would say, “In a minute.” I wish I had sat down.

teaser: My application was still in the drawer.
reflection: My application was still in the drawer. I had good reasons to wait, and some frightened ones. I wish I had told someone which were which, instead of pretending I had stopped wanting to learn.

teaser: I went to the rehearsal on Tuesday.
reflection: I went to the rehearsal on Tuesday. My voice shook through every song, and I returned the next week anyway. Those ordinary evenings became a whole part of my life that I nearly never met.

teaser: I knew her number without looking.
reflection: I knew her number without looking. Somehow that made calling feel less urgent, as if knowing where someone was meant we were still close. I kept the number longer than I kept the friendship.

teaser: The trip never became affordable.
reflection: The trip never became affordable. I do not blame myself for that. But there were afternoons in the courtyard I spent ashamed of staying, while my neighbors were making room for me at their table.

teaser: We stopped waiting for the perfect room.
reflection: We stopped waiting for the perfect room. We moved the chairs and invited everyone over. The music was uneven, the neighbors complained once, and I am glad we made a place for it.

teaser: We had supper together for forty years.
reflection: We had supper together for forty years. When I think about my life now, I keep hearing her put two plates on the table.

teaser: I answered every question except the quiet ones.
reflection: I answered every question except the quiet ones. My son would stay in the doorway after asking for the car keys. I wish I had noticed that he was sometimes waiting for an invitation to stay.

teaser: We argued about the dishes until the last week.
reflection: We argued about the dishes until the last week. I hope they remember the other things too: the spare keys, the soup, how none of us had to explain a bad day before sitting down.

teaser: He always slowed down at my gate.
reflection: He always slowed down at my gate. We talked about very little, which is how we eventually talked about everything. I had not expected another friendship to become so important after seventy.

teaser: I wanted her to call first.
reflection: I wanted her to call first. Years passed while I rehearsed how gracious I would be when she finally apologized. There were things I needed to say too, and I never made room for them.

teaser: My sister knew which train I took.
reflection: My sister knew which train I took. I wish I had stayed longer on those visits. Still, we made something of the hours we had, and I do not want my wanting more to erase them.

teaser: I kept waiting until I had more to give.
reflection: I kept waiting until I had more to give. There is money left. What hurts is remembering who needed help while I kept moving the amount that would finally make me feel secure.

teaser: I always made an extra portion.
reflection: I always made an extra portion. Sometimes nobody came, and I ate it the next day. Sometimes a person sat down who had not spoken to anyone all morning, and we had lunch.

teaser: I liked being thanked more than I admitted.
reflection: I liked being thanked more than I admitted. Once I began noticing that, I tried listening before offering help. Some people needed things I could not provide, and some needed me to stop deciding for them.

teaser: I gave advice when he asked for company.
reflection: I gave advice when he asked for company. It made me feel useful and let me leave quickly. I wish I had stayed through the awkward silence long enough to hear what he was trying to tell me.

teaser: The drill came back with a different handle.
reflection: The drill came back with a different handle. I laughed because it worked better. I liked seeing what people could make with something I owned, and eventually I stopped thinking of it as only mine.

teaser: I finally learned to leave some evenings empty.
reflection: I finally learned to leave some evenings empty. Saying yes to everyone had made me resent the people I loved. The help I could offer honestly was smaller, but I was there for it.

teaser: There were mornings when I hated getting up.
reflection: There were mornings when I hated getting up. Then someone would be relieved to see me. That mattered more than I knew.

teaser: There are still boxes without labels.
reflection: There are still boxes without labels. For years I imagined finishing would make me calm. Now I think of the people who learned beside me, and I am less afraid of leaving the last boxes to them.

teaser: I turned everything I enjoyed into a target.
reflection: I turned everything I enjoyed into a target. Even drawing on a Sunday became something I had to get better at. I miss the person who could fill a page and throw it away without feeling behind.

teaser: I became someone my friends could rely on.
reflection: I became someone my friends could rely on. It happened through small arrangements: arriving when I said I would, returning a call, telling the truth when I could not manage. I am proud of that life.

teaser: I never found one thing to be.
reflection: I never found one thing to be. I taught, repaired instruments, raised a child, and started over. Some changes were forced on me. Even so, there were moments in each life when I felt useful and awake.

teaser: I was good at looking certain.
reflection: I was good at looking certain. People trusted me, and I began treating every doubt as something shameful. I wish I had asked more questions while there were still people beside me who could answer.

teaser: I kept measuring our house against other houses.
reflection: I kept measuring our house against other houses. Meanwhile, people I loved were laughing in the kitchen. I was there with them, but part of me was always inspecting a life I did not have.

teaser: I was the least graceful person in the class.
reflection: I was the least graceful person in the class. Nobody needed me to be impressive there. I learned their names, lost the rhythm, tried again, and found a kind of ease I had missed for years.

teaser: I wanted a room of my own.
reflection: I wanted a room of my own. That was a reasonable thing to want. I wish I had not turned every photograph of someone else’s home into evidence that I had failed at being alive.

teaser: My brother never knew we were competing.
reflection: My brother never knew we were competing. He would tell me good news and I would spend the evening feeling smaller. I lost so many chances to be happy with him over a contest I invented.

teaser: Our games took most of Sunday.
reflection: Our games took most of Sunday. Some weeks I arrived still bitter about an argument or a rejection. I loved being expected there anyway, with my terrible strategies and extra snacks, without having to become cheerful before I could belong.

teaser: I still wanted people to like my work.
reflection: I still wanted people to like my work. I do not think that was wrong. But the afternoon my aunt fell asleep holding my hand mattered to me without anyone else ever seeing it.

teaser: The mint survived every winter.
reflection: The mint survived every winter. I would crush a leaf between my fingers before making tea. There were larger events in my life, of course, but that small familiar smell keeps returning to me now.

teaser: We listened to the rain through a leaking roof.
reflection: We listened to the rain through a leaking roof. I wanted the landlord to fix it, and I am still angry that he never did. I also remember my niece’s laugh when we ran out of bowls.

teaser: I hardly remember the routes without a stopwatch.
reflection: I hardly remember the routes without a stopwatch. There were trees changing color and friends talking beside me. I wish I had let a few mornings count for nothing except being outside together.

teaser: We opened the window while we worked.
reflection: We opened the window while we worked. The street would send us arguments, music, the bread delivery. It was an ordinary room and an ordinary life, and I liked the way I belonged inside it.

teaser: My child loved the cracked blue bowl.
reflection: My child loved the cracked blue bowl. I kept meaning to replace it. Now I remember how seriously he carried it to breakfast, and how a household can become yours through things nobody would choose from a shop.

teaser: The first loaf was almost inedible.
reflection: The first loaf was almost inedible. We ate the middle and made another the following week. I am glad I kept learning things that would never appear on a certificate or earn me anything.

teaser: She agreed to meet me for coffee.
reflection: She agreed to meet me for coffee. We did not repair twenty years that afternoon. I listened, badly at first, then better. I am grateful for that beginning even though I wanted more than she could give.

teaser: I could explain every hurtful thing I said.
reflection: I could explain every hurtful thing I said. I thought an explanation should make the hurt disappear. I wish I had spent less time defending my reasons and more time hearing what living with them had cost.

teaser: We started again with a bag of oranges.
reflection: We started again with a bag of oranges. Neither of us made a speech. Later we did talk about what happened, and it hurt, but by then we remembered why we had wanted each other in our lives.

teaser: Some people never answered my letters.
reflection: Some people never answered my letters. They had their reasons, and recovery did not entitle me to a reply. I kept changing what I could, with help, and learned to live without calling that change a bargain.

teaser: I told the story until I was blameless.
reflection: I told the story until I was blameless. Each time I left out another detail that made me uncomfortable. By the end, I had almost forgotten the apology I owed, though I had never stopped missing him.

teaser: I stopped waiting for the apology to arrive.
reflection: I stopped waiting for the apology to arrive. I kept the distance I needed and made a home with other people. Peace came slowly, and it did not require pretending that what happened had been all right.

teaser: I was happy.
reflection: I was happy. I still wanted more time. There are people I hadn’t finished loving, and small plans I was looking forward to keeping with them.

teaser: I do not need another grand chapter.
reflection: I do not need another grand chapter. I have loved people, made mistakes, learned their names again after losing touch. I would enjoy another morning, but I can look at the mornings I had without turning away.

teaser: I am still angry about leaving.
reflection: I am still angry about leaving. There are good things I can remember, and people who have been gentle with me. Neither makes this feel fair. I am trying to let gratitude and anger sit together.

teaser: There are pages I wish I could rewrite.
reflection: There are pages I wish I could rewrite. I cannot make those choices kinder now. I have told the truth about some of them, and I am still learning to stay with what the truth leaves unfinished.

teaser: Someone else can finish the glaze tests.
reflection: Someone else can finish the glaze tests. I left the notes where they can find them. I enjoyed the questions more than the answers, and I like imagining the workshop noisy again when I am gone.

teaser: I do not know how to say goodbye well.
reflection: I do not know how to say goodbye well. Sometimes I ask about the weather because I want an ordinary conversation. If that is what you remember, please know I was glad you were in the room.
